summary: @ornikar/jest-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's declared preinstall script runs setup.mjs, which is itself hex-identifier obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style _0x-prefixed identifiers with per-call string-lookup tables). setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/, extracts and chmod+x's the binary into a temp directory, and then execFileSync's math_init.js under that freshly downloaded runtime. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled JS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, shuffled numeric/string array n7gIxM indexed through a rotating accessor WV8StW) with no readable strings. This fires automatically on `npm install`. A jest configuration preset has no legitimate need for an alternate runtime or an opaque compiled payload. Running the payload under Bun rather than Node evades Node-based static analysis, and the two layers of obfuscation (loader and payload) intentionally block review of what the payload actually does on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
